localization.subtitle: Parametric EQ and MIDI control
localization.promotional_text: Build five-band EQ profiles, keep a local profile library and follow ADI-2 DAC volume changes. Native Mac controls, offline editing and demo mode included.
localization.description:
Build a five-band EQ profile on your Mac, keep your settings organized, and control your RME ADI-2 DAC through USB MIDI.

ADI-2 Companion is an independent native Mac app for listening setups that use an ADI-2 DAC. Shape each band with frequency, gain, Q and filter-type controls, and inspect the combined response curve before applying a profile to your output.

PROFILE EDITING
• Edit five parametric bands with a response graph and precise numeric controls.
• Import Equalizer APO or REW filter text, CSV filter data, and compatible JSON profiles.
• Review warnings when an import needs fewer bands or adjusted values.
• Keep profiles in a local library and export JSON copies to share or back up.
• Build and edit profiles offline without connecting hardware.

HARDWARE CONTROL
• Connect explicitly through USB MIDI and read the device settings before controls become available.
• Adjust output volume in 0.1 dB steps with keyboard and accessibility controls.
• Follow front-panel volume changes with a smoothly moving fader.
• Review EQ changes as a draft before choosing Apply to both output channels.
• Adjust live output and device parameters through native controls.

Explore the app in its clearly marked demo mode when your DAC is not connected. Demo mode sends no MIDI.

REQUIREMENTS AND CURRENT LIMITS
macOS 14 or later. Hardware control requires an RME ADI-2 DAC with compatible MIDI-control firmware, a USB connection, and MIDI Control enabled on the device. The app does not record or process playback audio, change the Mac's sample rate, or turn the DAC on remotely.

Hardware validation covers an ADI-2 DAC on Apple silicon with macOS 27.2, including USB 81 / DSP 62 firmware. ADI-2 Pro and ADI-2/4 Pro hardware, Intel runtime behavior and other OS combinations have not been qualified with this Mac app.

No accounts, advertising or telemetry. Profiles stay on your Mac unless you export or share them yourself.

Independent software. Not affiliated with or endorsed by RME. Product names identify compatible hardware and belong to their respective owners.
localization.review_notes:
PREPARATION STATUS
These notes describe planned version 1.0.0 build 2, which has not yet been built, signed, uploaded or hardware-qualified. Build 1 was delivered, processed and attached to the existing version draft with two screenshots and a physical-camera hardware interaction video. No App Review submission or public release has occurred. Reconcile these notes and assets with the final validated build before submission.

ADI-2 Companion is an independent local macOS EQ editor and USB MIDI controller for ADI-2 DAC owners and people preparing five-band EQ profiles offline. It is a paid upfront, one-time purchase with no in-app purchases or subscriptions. It is not RME's official Remote application. The icon and interface artwork are original.

No account or reviewer login is needed. There is no subscription flow, network backend, audio capture, privileged helper or driver installer. The app uses App Sandbox and user-selected file read/write access. Its local profile library stays inside its sandbox container.

WITHOUT HARDWARE
Choose Explore demo in the sidebar, or Device > Explore Demo in the menu bar. Keep the demo banner visible. Select an output and edit the EQ bands; Apply in demo updates simulated state only. Import/Export and local profile Save/Load use local files. Choose Local profiles in the sidebar to open the Profiles page. Loading a local profile creates a draft and sends no MIDI.

WITH HARDWARE
Use a physical ADI-2 DAC connected to the Mac by USB. Enable MIDI Control on the device; the menu wording depends on firmware. Select the DAC's MIDI endpoint and click Connect. Fresh output/EQ state is read before writes are enabled. Sync reads hardware settings again. Output volume and enabled live parameter controls write immediately. EQ band edits remain drafts until Apply EQ to Both Channels is chosen.

VALIDATION RECORDED
On Apple silicon and macOS 27.2, the physical DAC completed discovery, fresh 219-parameter reads and a 0.1 dB Phones-volume reduction/restoration with readback. The owner confirmed smooth physical-knob feedback. Distribution-signed build 1 passed a neutral EQ Apply and fresh readback. Firmware was observed at USB 80 / DSP 55 and later USB 81 / DSP 62. These observations do not qualify Pro/2/4 hardware, Intel runtime, unplug/replug, every parameter or arbitrary EQ transitions, and they do not validate the build 2 scope change.

The first paid Mac release excludes persistent device preset/setup operations. Include the exact final app revision, tested Mac/OS/device/firmware list, required hardware video and actual review contact in the finished submission.
